distinguishing_features: Uses a non-contact high-gradient magnetic field rather than chemical dosing, monitoring, thermal retuning, or anti-agglomerant treatment
Targets fine, magnetically responsive iron-bearing particles below conventional screen or bag-filter size limits
Separates magnetic fines directly from a flowing rare-earth leachate stream without adding reagent or consuming filter media
Applies a magnetic-gradient force mechanism to impurity removal in a rare-earth hydrometallurgical stream
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Selectively remove fine iron and thorium impurities from rare-earth leachate without adding separation reagents or relying on conventional filtration that can miss or clog on sub-50-micrometer particles.
parsed.viable_reason: High-gradient magnetic separation is physically feasible for iron-bearing fines, but thorium ions and ordinary thorium precipitates are generally too weakly magnetic for the proposed setup to capture reliably without an unspecified magnetic conditioning or precipitation step.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The candidate's use of a non-contact magnetic-gradient capture mechanism for selective impurity removal is mechanically distinct from all three cited operating-point, dosing, or additive-retuning approaches and is not a routine application of those closest methods.
